facts.fact: CPM stands for Cost Per Mille, and 'mille' is Latin for thousand, so CPM is the price an advertiser pays for one thousand views or impressions of an ad.
facts.quote: When you hear people in advertising talk about **CPM**, they're talking about **Cost Per Mille**. It’s a fancy-sounding term, but "mille" is just Latin for "thousand."

facts.fact: The page gives the CPM formula as (Total Campaign Cost / Total Impressions) x 1,000.
facts.quote: > **CPM Formula: (Total Campaign Cost / Total Impressions) x 1,000 = CPM**

facts.fact: An impression is defined on the page as one single time an ad appears on a screen.
facts.quote: An impression is one single time your ad appears on a screen. So, 1,000 impressions means your ad was displayed 1,000 times.

facts.fact: In Adwave's illustrative example, a local business spending $300 on a TV ad campaign with 20,000 impressions would pay a CPM of $15.
facts.quote: You spend **$300**, and in return, your commercial is shown **20,000** times to households in your area.

facts.fact: Adwave's example calculates the CPM as ($300 / 20,000 Impressions) x 1,000 = $15 CPM.
